summary: This is a set of architecture tests that enforce code organization rules for a Laravel application. It ensures that different parts of the codebase (controllers, models, repositories, etc.) only interact with each other in specific, allowed ways — for example, models should only be used in repositories, and certain debug functions should never be used in production code.

explanations.2: The `expect()` method specifies which part of the codebase we're testing — in this case, all files in the 'App\Http\Controllers' namespace.
explanations.3: The `not->toUse()` modifier inverts the rule, so this line says controllers must NOT directly use Laravel's Request class.
explanations.8: The `toOnlyBeUsedOn()` method restricts which parts of the code are allowed to import or reference models — here, only repositories can use them.
explanations.9: The `toOnlyUse()` method whitelist what this namespace can depend on, so repositories are only allowed to use models and the Illuminate Database library.
explanations.13: This says repositories can only be imported and used by controllers, enforcing a one-way dependency flow.
explanations.17: Instead of a namespace, we can test specific function names as a list — here we're checking that debug functions like `dd()` and `dump()` aren't being called.
explanations.23: The `ignoring()` method creates an exception to the rule — facades can be used everywhere EXCEPT we're allowing the Providers folder to use them without triggering a test failure.
